value: The two groups of smokers differed in BOLD responses to pleasant and cigarette-related stimuli in the dorsal striatum, medial prefrontal cortex, and other brain regions.
Group 1 had larger responses to pleasant pictures than to cigarette-related pictures, whereas Group 2 showed the opposite pattern.

These results suggest that Group 2 had enhanced responses to cigarette-related cues relative to pleasant stimuli and was characterized by low reward sensitivity, whereas Group 1 was characterized by high reward sensitivity.

description.value: The study used prequit fMRI to examine whether baseline brain responses to pleasant and cigarette-related cues differed between two subgroups of smokers and predicted smoking cessation outcomes.

spans.text: In the current study, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to measure baseline brain responses of smokers interested in quitting.

caption.value: Brain Regions With Significant Group × Picture Category Interaction

footer.value: Note. B = bilateral; BA = Brodmann area, FDR = false discovery rate; Hem = hemisphere, L = left, R = right. These brain areas were identified using a group (high reward sensitivity, low reward sensitivity) × picture category (cigarette-related, pleasant) voxelwise generalized linear model on all voxels that were not used to divide the smokers into groups. Location is expressed in Talairach coordinates (mm) and is presented for the center of gravity of each activation cluster. Fmax = F(3,159) statistic for the group × picture category interaction from the peak voxel in each cluster (all voxelwise ps < .0001, p[FDR] < .01).
